message:
It took me 18 months to make a board game that quizzers would enjoy, it's ready for you to buy!

If that one line is enough for you, then you can just head over to the shop page already and skip the rest of the email where I try to convince you why this game is the greatest thing since sliced bread whatever is the last greatest thing.

Oh, you really want me to pitch to you? Sure thing, read on-

Hi, I'm Ajay Poonia - if we've met at a quiz then you know me. If not, I'm a quizmaster with 15+ years of experience of hosting quizzes with schools, colleges, corporates, government organizations, and TV channels. Here's my YouTube.

Now, while hosting quizzes is a lot of fun, I’ve always been bothered by the impermanence of a quiz. It is organized in an auditorium or a pub on a certain day, I ask a few questions, you answer even fewer (hehe), and then it's over. So, I wanted to stretch the possibility of how high quality quizzing can be experienced, for longer and at your convenience. After a lot of thinking and talking to people (including some of you), and some more thinking, I arrived at a solution - a board game around quizzing. And not just a basic luck based, single mechanic, know-it-all-wins kind of a game. That's boring and easy to make.
The board game I, along with my co-designer (Bhushan Patel), set out to create had to bring the characteristics of any top quality quiz - great content, a fair bit of strategy, and a lot of fun. I'm pleased to tell you, we've managed to do just that. It took a team of 16 people 18 months and 150+ demo sessions (I stopped journaling about it after 80 such sessions) with over 600 people across India belonging to diverse age groups (seriously, class 4 students love it as much as 65 year-olds and everyone in between).

After a lot of trials, errors, and tweaks, we've managed to create an amazing twist to quizzing. It's called — drumrolls — Trivia Pirates. And, the best part, it comes with a Netflix-style question streaming
